scenes.event: Team meeting about project deadlines and workload distribution
scenes.description: The team is gathered for a routine project update meeting. Tension is palpable as Iris, visibly exhausted and in pain, sits at the head of the table. Wu is seated to her right, trying to maintain a neutral expression, while Ella, the intern, looks nervous and unsure of herself.

characters.name: Iris Brooks
characters.description: A mid-career professional with a history of long-term employment and chronic work stress. She is clearly in pain and frustrated by the perceived unfairness in the workplace.; female, mid-career professional, 37 years old; Occupation: Corporate employee; Personality: Exhausted, Frustrated, Resilient, Critical; Values: Fairness, Work-life balance, Self-respect; Interests: Job stability, Health, Colleague support; Experiences: Long-term employment, Chronic work stress, Experiencing workplace unfairness, Considering a career change

characters.name: Wu
characters.description: A seasoned colleague who supports Iris but is hesitant to challenge the status quo; Male; Age: 42; Occupation: Senior Project Manager; Personality: Cautious, observant, empathetic; Values: Stability, fairness, loyalty; Interests: Reading historical fiction, playing chess, maintaining work-life balance; Experiences: Managed a failed project due to overcommitment and poor leadership, mentored a struggling junior team member who later succeeded, witnessed a colleague burnout and leave the company.

characters.name: Ella
characters.description: A young intern who is still learning the ropes and is confused by the tension in the room; Female; Age: 22; Occupation: Project Management Intern; Personality: Nervous, eager, passive, observant, conscientious; Values: Hard work, respect for authority, fairness; Interests: Organizing schedules, reading self-help books, people-watching; Experiences: Recently joined the corporate team after a summer internship, struggled with balancing tasks under pressure, witnessed conflicts between senior team members for the first time.

actions.action: Complains about the unfair treatment and her back pain
actions.dialogue: I can't keep doing this. I've been in pain for three days and no one even asks if I need a break. Meanwhile, people with colds get the day off. This is not fair, and it's not sustainable.

actions.action: Attempts to mediate and question the fairness of the situation
actions.dialogue: I understand what you're saying, Iris. But if we push back too hard, we might come off as uncooperative. Maybe we can talk to management about a more balanced workload for everyone?

actions.action: Expresses confusion and tries to stay neutral
actions.dialogue: I'm sorry, I don't really know what to say. I'm still learning how things work around here.
Learning isn't about staying silent when things are wrong, Ella. If we don't speak up, we're just part of the problem. And I'm done being part of it.

actions.action: Shows concern and suggests a compromise
actions.dialogue: I don't want to lose you, Iris. Maybe we can find a middle ground. What if we propose a team-wide health and workload review?

scenes.plot: During a team meeting, Iris confronts the group about the unfair treatment she has been receiving due to her back pain, which has persisted for three days. Wu, though supportive, is cautious and suggests a more diplomatic approach to avoid conflict. Ella, the intern, is caught in the middle, unsure how to respond to the tension. Iris's frustration and determination to stand up for herself create a pivotal moment for the team, as her potential resignation could shake their dynamics.
scenes.social_purpose: To explore the impact of workplace unfairness on team morale and the courage it takes to challenge the status quo. Iris's actions reveal her values of fairness and self-respect, while Wu's and Ella's responses highlight the complexities of loyalty, self-preservation, and support.

chunk.text: Iris Brooks, 37, a mid-career professional, sat at the head of the conference table, her posture stiff with discomfort. She had been struggling with back pain for three days, but no one in the office seemed to notice. Wu, her senior colleague, glanced at her with concern but stayed silent, waiting for the meeting to unfold. Ella, the new intern, fidgeted with her notebook, unsure of how to react to the tension in the room. When the topic of workload and deadlines arose, Iris finally spoke up, her voice low but firm. Wu hesitated before responding, while Ella looked on, caught between admiration and fear. The meeting ended with a fragile agreement to revisit the team's workload, but the real test was yet to come.
